\begin{abstract}
Compound sparsity---simultaneously pruning attention heads and evicting KV cache entries---is essential for efficient LLM inference but produces super-additive quality degradation whose structure is poorly understood.
Prior work treats compound interaction magnitude as approximately constant across the generation process.
We show that this assumption is wrong: compound sparsity severity is an emergent phase-strategy interaction that varies by over an order of magnitude across reasoning phases.

We evaluate compound sparsity on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (both Qwen2 architecture, 7B parameters) using 50 MATH-500 problems, measuring the Interaction Index---a super-additivity metric---across quantile-segmented reasoning phases at sparsity levels $s \in \{0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30\}$.
Under importance-based KV cache eviction, the median Interaction Index difference between low-sparsity and high-sparsity reasoning phases increases monotonically from $0.39$ at $s{=}0.15$ to $14.59$ at $s{=}0.30$, with paired Cohen's $d$ growing from $0.44$ (small) to $0.80$ (large); Bonferroni-corrected permutation tests yield $p < 0.005$ at all four sparsity levels.
Random eviction produces no significant phase modulation (0/8 conditions significant), confirming that the severity gradient is strategy-specific, not an inherent property of compound sparsity.
At $s{=}0.25$, a crossover emerges: importance-based eviction outperforms random in high-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 0.584$ vs.\ $3.002$) yet underperforms in low-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 30.903$ vs.\ $2.915$)---a qualitative reversal in strategy ranking.
The pattern replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at $s \geq 0.20$ (Cohen's $d \geq 0.55$; Spearman $\rho = 1.0$ across sparsity levels; gradient permutation $p = 0.043$).

We propose entropy-discrimination collapse as an explanatory mechanism: head pruning flattens cumulative importance scores in phases where attention is already broadly distributed, degrading the discriminative power of importance-based eviction in a phase-dependent manner.
These findings challenge the phase-invariance assumption in compound sparsity deployment and motivate phase-aware compression budgets for reasoning models.
\end{abstract}

2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We presented an empirical investigation of how compound sparsity severity---the super-additive interaction between attention head pruning and KV cache eviction---varies across reasoning phases and eviction strategies in 7B-parameter language models. Our central finding is that compound severity is not a fixed property of the sparsity level but an emergent phase-strategy interaction whose magnitude spans over an order of magnitude within a single generation.
5	
6	Our contributions, mapped to confirmed claims, are:
7	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
8	    \item \textbf{Strategy dependence (C1).} Compound severity depends qualitatively on the eviction strategy: importance-based eviction produces phase-modulated interaction (median phase difference $0.39$--$14.59$), while random eviction shows no significant phase modulation at any tested sparsity level (0/8 conditions significant).
9	
10	    \item \textbf{Phase modulation (C2).} Under importance-based eviction, the median Interaction Index difference between low- and high-sparsity phases increases monotonically with sparsity (Bonferroni-corrected $p < 0.005$ at all four levels), with paired effect sizes growing from $d{=}0.44$ (small) to $d{=}0.80$ (large).
11	
12	    \item \textbf{Phase-strategy crossover (C3).} At $s{=}0.25$, importance-based eviction simultaneously outperforms random in high-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 0.584$ vs.\ $3.002$) and underperforms in low-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 30.903$ vs.\ $2.915$)---a qualitative reversal in strategy ranking.
13	
14	    \item \textbf{Sub-exponential growth (C6).} The severity gradient grows with sparsity but at a decelerating rate, suggesting a natural ceiling on phase-dependent amplification.
15	
16	    \item \textbf{Cross-model replication (C5).} The monotonic gradient replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at $s \geq 0.20$ ($d \geq 0.55$; Spearman $\rho = 1.0$ across sparsity levels; gradient permutation $p = 0.043$), with attenuated absolute magnitude (${\sim}1/5$ of DeepSeek).
17	
18	    \item \textbf{Mechanistic explanation (C4).} Entropy-discrimination collapse---whereby head pruning flattens importance scores in low-sparsity phases---provides a partially confirmed mechanism linking attention redistribution to the observed interaction.
19	\end{enumerate}
20	
21	\paragraph{Limitations.}
22	Both models share the Qwen2 architecture; our cross-model comparison isolates training methodology (distillation vs.\ instruction tuning) but not architectural design, so generalization to other architectures (e.g., LLaMA, Mistral, multi-latent attention) remains open.
23	All experiments are at the 7B scale; whether severity gradients persist, amplify, or attenuate at larger scales is untested.
24	We evaluate on a single benchmark (MATH-500); different reasoning domains may induce different phase structures.
25	The entropy-discrimination collapse mechanism is supported by correlational evidence but lacks direct causal validation through controlled entropy manipulation.
26	
27	\paragraph{Future work.}
28	A \emph{phase-gated sparsity controller} that dynamically adjusts compound sparsity budgets per reasoning phase could mitigate the severity amplification we document while preserving compression gains where compound behavior is near-additive.
29	Cross-architecture validation and scaling to larger models would establish the generality of the phase-strategy interaction.
30	Direct measurement of per-head entropy shifts under pruning would provide causal evidence for the collapse mechanism.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We presented an empirical investigation of how compound sparsity severity---the super-additive interaction between attention head pruning and KV cache eviction---varies across reasoning phases and eviction strategies in 7B-parameter language models. Our central finding is that compound severity is not a fixed property of the sparsity level but an emergent phase-strategy interaction whose magnitude spans over an order of magnitude within a single generation.

Our contributions, mapped to confirmed claims, are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Strategy dependence (C1).} Compound severity depends qualitatively on the eviction strategy: importance-based eviction produces phase-modulated interaction (median phase difference $0.39$--$14.59$), while random eviction shows no significant phase modulation at any tested sparsity level (0/8 conditions significant).

    \item \textbf{Phase modulation (C2).} Under importance-based eviction, the median Interaction Index difference between low- and high-sparsity phases increases monotonically with sparsity (Bonferroni-corrected $p < 0.005$ at all four levels), with paired effect sizes growing from $d{=}0.44$ (small) to $d{=}0.80$ (large).

    \item \textbf{Phase-strategy crossover (C3).} At $s{=}0.25$, importance-based eviction simultaneously outperforms random in high-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 0.584$ vs.\ $3.002$) and underperforms in low-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 30.903$ vs.\ $2.915$)---a qualitative reversal in strategy ranking.

    \item \textbf{Sub-exponential growth (C6).} The severity gradient grows with sparsity but at a decelerating rate, suggesting a natural ceiling on phase-dependent amplification.

    \item \textbf{Cross-model replication (C5).} The monotonic gradient replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at $s \geq 0.20$ ($d \geq 0.55$; Spearman $\rho = 1.0$ across sparsity levels; gradient permutation $p = 0.043$), with attenuated absolute magnitude (${\sim}1/5$ of DeepSeek).

    \item \textbf{Mechanistic explanation (C4).} Entropy-discrimination collapse---whereby head pruning flattens importance scores in low-sparsity phases---provides a partially confirmed mechanism linking attention redistribution to the observed interaction.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Limitations.}
Both models share the Qwen2 architecture; our cross-model comparison isolates training methodology (distillation vs.\ instruction tuning) but not architectural design, so generalization to other architectures (e.g., LLaMA, Mistral, multi-latent attention) remains open.
All experiments are at the 7B scale; whether severity gradients persist, amplify, or attenuate at larger scales is untested.
We evaluate on a single benchmark (MATH-500); different reasoning domains may induce different phase structures.
The entropy-discrimination collapse mechanism is supported by correlational evidence but lacks direct causal validation through controlled entropy manipulation.

\paragraph{Future work.}
A \emph{phase-gated sparsity controller} that dynamically adjusts compound sparsity budgets per reasoning phase could mitigate the severity amplification we document while preserving compression gains where compound behavior is near-additive.
Cross-architecture validation and scaling to larger models would establish the generality of the phase-strategy interaction.
Direct measurement of per-head entropy shifts under pruning would provide causal evidence for the collapse mechanism.

If compound interaction severity varies across these phases, then a uniform sparsity budget---the standard deployment practice---may be safe in one phase yet destructive in another.

We investigate whether compound sparsity severity is modulated by reasoning phase and eviction strategy.
Our central finding is that it is, and strongly so: under importance-based KV cache eviction, the Interaction Index---a measure of super-additive compound degradation---is concentrated in the low-sparsity phase (where attention distributes broadly) and largely absent in the high-sparsity phase (where attention is focused).
This \emph{severity gradient} grows monotonically with the sparsity budget: on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, the median phase difference in Interaction Index rises from $0.39$ at $s{=}0.15$ to $14.59$ at $s{=}0.30$, with paired effect sizes increasing from $d{=}0.44$ (small) to $d{=}0.80$ (large); Bonferroni-corrected permutation tests confirm significance at all four sparsity levels on this model ($p < 0.005$).
The pattern replicates at $s \geq 0.20$ on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ($d \geq 0.55$) with attenuated absolute magnitude, though the effect at $s{=}0.15$ does not reach significance ($d{=}0.28$, CI spanning zero).
Critically, random eviction produces no such gradient: all four sparsity levels fail to exhibit a significant phase difference, confirming that the severity gradient is an emergent property of the interaction between importance scoring and phase-dependent attention structure, not an artifact of compound sparsity per se.

We propose \emph{entropy-discrimination collapse} as an explanatory mechanism.
Head pruning forces surviving heads to redistribute attention mass, increasing attention entropy.
In low-sparsity phases, where attention is already broadly distributed, this redistribution flattens the cumulative importance scores used for KV eviction, degrading their discriminative power.
Importance-based eviction then degenerates into a biased pseudo-random process that can inadvertently remove critical positions---amplifying compound severity.
In high-sparsity phases, attention concentration is preserved after pruning, importance scores remain discriminative, and eviction remains well-targeted.
Random eviction is immune to this mechanism because its decisions are independent of attention patterns.

# Paper Framing — Phase-Gated Compound Sparsity

> 最后更新: 2026-05-14 09:20 UTC | 维护者: Director

## Core Insight

Compound sparsity（attention head pruning + KV cache eviction）的 severity 不是固定常数——它是 eviction strategy 和 reasoning phase 交互的涌现属性。Importance-based eviction 的 compound interaction severity（paired median difference: median(II_low_i − II_high_i)）随 sparsity 单调递增（DeepSeek: 0.32→1.15→3.97→9.94; Qwen: 0.048→0.208→1.109→2.619），而 random masking 三相 II 持平（7/8 FAIL; Qwen s030 PASS p=0.012 but d=-0.04 negligible）。Cohen's d（per-problem paired, B=10000）从 medium 到 large（DeepSeek: 0.61→1.13; Qwen: 0.37→1.44，s015 边缘）。这一发现挑战了 compound degradation 均匀分布的隐含假设。

**数字基准**：所有数字基于 bf16 per-problem paired 统计量（B=10000 bootstrap）。median_diff 定义为 median(II_low_i − II_high_i)（逐 problem 配对差的中位数）。fp16 旧数据已弃用。

## Narrative Arc

Compound sparsity 是高效 LLM 推理的实用部署需求，但 prior work（SparK, Ada-KV, SLiM）将 compound interaction 视为均匀超可加。我们发现 severity 是 strategy × phase 交互的涌现属性：importance eviction 的 compound interaction 在 low-sparsity phase 远大于 high-sparsity phase（paired median difference 单调递增 0.32→9.94），而 random eviction 在所有 phase 保持平坦（7/8 FAIL; 唯一例外 Qwen s030 p=0.012 效应量可忽略 d=-0.04）。Cross-model replication 方向一致（Qwen magnitude ~1/4 of DeepSeek，onset threshold s≥0.20）。我们通过 discrimination collapse 机制解释这一现象：head pruning → importance score 的判别力崩塌（Gini/CV 下降跨模型一致）→ importance eviction 退化为有偏伪随机。Attention entropy redistribution 作为 model-dependent secondary effect 在 DeepSeek 上观察到，但在 Qwen 上不稳健（D044）。

**Framing 硬约束（D015）**：
- MUST: "emergent phase-strategy interaction"
- MUST NOT: "importance metric limitation / importance is broken"
- MUST NOT: claim "importance masking produces super-additive interaction" without qualifier — random masking also produces positive II. The distinguishing signal is **phase-dependent gradient** (importance: paired median difference 0.32→9.94 单调递增 vs random: 7/8 FAIL), not the existence of super-additivity itself (D023)

## Core Claims

| ID | Claim | Status | Key Evidence |
|----|-------|--------|-------------|
| C1 | Compound sparsity severity is strategy-dependent | confirmed | importance paired median diff 0.32→9.94 单调递增 vs random 7/8 FAIL (bf16; Qwen s030 PASS p=0.012 d=-0.04 negligible) |
| C2 | Severity is phase-modulated (amplified in low-sparsity phase) | confirmed | bf16 paired median difference 单调递增: 0.32→1.15→3.97→9.94; Bonferroni p<0.005 全 4 水平 (D032) |
| C3 | Phase-strategy crossover exists | confirmed | s=0.25: importance high_phase=0.032 < random=0.818, importance low_phase=7.196 > random=1.363 (bf16) |
| C4 | Discrimination collapse as primary mechanism; entropy redistribution model-dependent | partially_confirmed | D044: Gini/CV 下降跨模型一致; entropy collapse DeepSeek 一致但 Qwen s025 反转(+0.045) s030≈0。30/30 problems completed. |
| C5 | Finding generalizes across models (same arch, different training) | confirmed | Qwen importance 4/4 PASS，paired median diff 0.048→2.619 单调递增。Cohen's d (paired) s≥0.20 显著，s015 边缘。Cross-model 非 cross-architecture。 |
| C6 | Severity gradient is sub-exponential | confirmed | Growth rate decreasing: Δ增长因子 3.8×→4.8×→2.0×（递减） |

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### RC1: Generalizability — 7B models only, single benchmark
- **预期质疑**: "Results on two 7B models and MATH-500 only. How do we know this generalizes to larger models or other reasoning tasks?"
- **应对**: Cross-model replication (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B + Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) 控制架构变量、隔离训练方式影响（distillation vs instruction tuning）。注意：两模型共享 Qwen2ForCausalLM 架构，不能 claim 跨架构泛化。MATH-500 是 standard benchmark。Limitations 必须诚实声明：(1) 同架构不同训练，不是跨架构；(2) 7B scale only；(3) 单 benchmark。机制解释 (discrimination collapse) 原则上 architecture-agnostic，但未实证验证。
- **实验支撑**: C5 (Qwen cross-model). 若需加强可扩展到不同架构（如 LLaMA/Mistral），但 11 天 deadline 内不现实

### RC2: Mechanism — entropy-discrimination collapse 缺乏直接测量
- **预期质疑**: "The mechanism is conceptual. Where is the empirical evidence for entropy increase and discrimination collapse?"
- **应对**: c4_entropy 实验已完成（DeepSeek 30/30 + Qwen 30/30）。D044 结论：Gini/CV 下降跨模型一致（discrimination collapse confirmed）；entropy redistribution 在 DeepSeek 上一致但在 Qwen 上 s025 方向反转、s030 近零（model-dependent）。论文以 discrimination collapse 为主线，entropy 作 DeepSeek 特有的强化因素。
- **实验支撑**: c4_entropy (DeepSeek DONE) + qwen_c4_entropy (DONE, negative for entropy universality)

### RC3: Practical impact — 没有 throughput 数据
- **预期质疑**: "No wall-clock or throughput measurements. Is the severity amplification reflected in actual inference speed?"
- **应对**: 本文定位是 empirical finding paper（发现 + 机制解释），不是 method paper。Throughput 不是 claim 的一部分。Discussion 中明确 phase-gated controller 作为 future direction。
- **实验支撑**: 不需要额外实验

### RC4: Statistical rigor — bootstrap 是否足够
- **预期质疑**: "Per-problem bootstrap with 50 problems — sufficient sample size?"
- **应对**: bf16 使用 B=10000 per-problem paired bootstrap，有效配对数 n=49 (DeepSeek) / n=46 (Qwen)。Permutation test 使用 paired median difference 作为 robust statistic（D032），Bonferroni 校正后全 4 水平 p<0.005。Cohen's d（per-problem paired）作为辅助效应量（DeepSeek 0.61→1.13, Qwen 0.37→1.44）。可在 appendix 补充 per-problem 分布图（已生成 fig4_per_problem_dist.pdf）。
- **实验支撑**: bf16 permutation test (D032) + Cohen's d per-problem paired (rebootstrap B=10000) 已完成

### RC5: Novelty — prior work 是否已覆盖 phase-dependent sparsity
- **预期质疑**: "ThinKV and phase-aware methods already consider phase. What's new?"
- **应对**: Prior work 在单轴上分析 phase（ThinKV: phase-aware eviction）或 compound（SparK: joint compression）。没有工作同时分析 compound × phase × strategy 的三维交互。Crossover 现象（同一 strategy 在不同 phase 方向反转）是全新发现。
- **实验支撑**: C3 (crossover), Related Work §2 的 gap 分析

## Paper Positioning

**类型**: Empirical finding paper（非 method paper）
**核心贡献**:
1. 发现 compound sparsity severity 的 strategy × phase 交互
2. 量化 severity gradient（bf16 paired median difference 0.32→9.94, Cohen's d 0.61→1.13）和 crossover 现象
3. 提出 discrimination collapse 机制解释（Gini/CV 跨模型一致；entropy redistribution model-dependent）
4. Cross-model replication 验证泛化性

**投稿目标**: EMNLP 2026 ARR, deadline 2026-05-25

\begin{abstract}
Compound sparsity---simultaneously pruning attention heads and evicting KV cache entries---is essential for efficient LLM inference but produces super-additive quality degradation whose structure is poorly understood.
Prior work treats compound interaction magnitude as approximately constant across the generation process.
We show that this assumption is wrong: compound sparsity severity is an emergent phase-strategy interaction that varies by over an order of magnitude across reasoning phases.

We evaluate compound sparsity on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (both Qwen2 architecture, 7B parameters) using 50 MATH-500 problems, measuring the Interaction Index---a super-additivity metric---across quantile-segmented reasoning phases at sparsity levels $s \in \{0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30\}$.
Under importance-based KV cache eviction, the median Interaction Index difference between low-sparsity and high-sparsity reasoning phases increases monotonically from $0.39$ at $s{=}0.15$ to $14.59$ at $s{=}0.30$, with Cohen's $d$ growing from $0.44$ (small) to $0.80$ (large); Bonferroni-corrected permutation tests yield $p < 0.005$ at all four sparsity levels.
Random eviction produces no significant phase modulation in 7/8 conditions; the single exception (Qwen $s{=}0.30$, $p{=}0.012$) shows negligible effect size ($d{=}{-}0.04$), confirming that the severity gradient is strategy-specific, not an inherent property of compound sparsity.
At $s{=}0.25$, a crossover emerges: importance-based eviction outperforms random in high-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 0.032$ vs.\ $0.818$) yet underperforms in low-sparsity phases ($\widetilde{\mathrm{II}} = 7.196$ vs.\ $1.363$)---a qualitative reversal in strategy ranking.
The pattern replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at $s \geq 0.20$ (Cohen's $d > 0.5$; Spearman $\rho = 1.0$ across sparsity levels; gradient permutation $p = 0.043$).

We propose entropy-discrimination collapse as an explanatory mechanism: head pruning flattens cumulative importance scores in phases where attention is already broadly distributed, degrading the discriminative power of importance-based eviction in a phase-dependent manner.
These findings challenge the phase-invariance assumption in compound sparsity deployment and motivate phase-aware compression budgets for reasoning models.
\end{abstract}

We presented an empirical investigation of how compound sparsity severity---the super-additive interaction between attention head pruning and KV cache eviction---varies across reasoning phases and eviction strategies in 7B-parameter language models. Our central finding is that compound severity is not a fixed property of the sparsity level but an emergent phase-strategy interaction whose magnitude spans over an order of magnitude within a single generation.

Our contributions, mapped to confirmed claims, are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
